figures.title: Speech-intention decoding in 13 components: what the field reports
figures.subtitle: Share of ledger entries in which each component is recorded: silent speech, brain-to-text and lip reading
figures.note: 8,995 ledger entries, each paper normalized into the same 13 components. A low share means papers rarely report or study it.
figures.caption: Every speech-intention decoder, whatever its sensor, can be described by the same 13 components: what the user does in training and in use, what is sensed, how it is decoded, what comes out, how the user confirms or corrects it, and how it is evaluated. The field concentrates on sensing, decoding and evaluation; confirmation, correction, runtime aids and training-only supervision are almost never reported. Counts come from the maintainer's normalized paper ledger (spec v2.1); a component counts as recorded when the ledger holds at least one fact for it.
